findings.detail: The changelog describes a new funded daily top-up to 110% of a baseline. For machines with under seven days of history, the baseline is a cohort average. Qualification needs only macOS 27 or later, two downloaded models, saved consent and 90% uptime. Sessions and identity aliases are merged, but the entry does not show that the top-up depends on served inference, or that the machine is a unique physical Mac. T-055 already says App Attest aliases prove credential continuity, not unique hardware or capacity. An operator (ADV-001) could therefore register many fresh or low-traffic machines, or machines running on borrowed identities, keep them connected, and draw cohort-based floor payments from the shared pool until the cap is reached. The pool cap bounds the loss. Uptime, model-inventory and consent inputs come from provider reports or the provider-authenticated socket. The new admin funding, repair and backfill endpoints also touch A-009 and TB-006. No threat entry covers reward-fraud, cohort-baseline gaming or these admin controls. Fix: add a threat entry for payout abuse and its mitigations. Before enabling payments, consider requiring minimum served-token or work evidence, per-account and per-machine caps, a cohort minimum size, and an audit trail for backfill and repair.
